solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One leaves intact vessel in warehouse

indicators.note: one leaving a word means that letter departs from it, so the I is taken out

parts.note: something intact is entire, whole
one is the Roman numeral I
a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: Someone describes a warehouse where a container survives unscathed while one of its contents departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes I out of ENTIRE, leaving ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading port or depot where goods are stored before re-export, a kind of warehouse.

clue.text: Board rescue vessel after English doctor

indicators.note: after places the vessel behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
Noah's ark rescued creatures from the Flood

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb aboard a lifeboat behind an English medic.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go on board a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: City codebreaker briefly identified

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Alan Turing was the Bletchley Park codebreaker

explanation.surface: A city is identified by a codebreaker in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final G from TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Aim to secure new life in London suburb

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the aim encloses the other letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of life are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to start a new life somewhere in the London suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on life, and 'to secure' has the aim hold the result between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is a borough on the northern outskirts of London.

clue.text: Meteorological phenomenon commander took in, in leaving war zone

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding

indicators.note: leaving means the second in departs from the word

parts.note: included means took in
the word in is taken as written, the letters removed
the front is the zone of fighting in a war

explanation.surface: A weather event the commander absorbed while pulling out of the battle area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IN from INCLUDED, giving CLUDED.
explanation.definitionFit: An occluded front is a weather front formed when a cold front overtakes a warm one.

clue.text: Maybe Smollett's books reflected prejudice

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the crossword's usual books
bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A critic suggests that the novelist's books mirror his own prejudices.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist; 'Maybe' marks the definition as one example of his name. 'reflected' turns the books round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias was Smollett's given name, so the name is an example of what Smollett is called.

clue.text: Old boy and girl taking over American patent

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
US means American

explanation.surface: A former pupil and a girl taking over an American patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like an invention right but is the adjective meaning plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plainly evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Urgent aim to protect little sibling

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shelter, so the sibling goes inside

parts.note: intent means aim
sis is a shortened sister

explanation.surface: A pressing goal of shielding a younger brother or sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent means demanding attention persistently, and so pressing or urgent.

clue.text: Most meagre spring initially spilling into others

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: into places that letter inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: initially means the first letter only of the word spilling

explanation.surface: The thinnest trickle of a spring at first spills into the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it picks the S of spring, but spring is SPA and the S comes from spilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, so sparsest is the most meagre.

clue.text: Glaring error primarily confronted by advocates generally

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers, advocates in general

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter only of the word error is used

parts.note: faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A blatant mistake is challenged by lawyers in general.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bar is the legal profession of barristers as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A barefaced lie is shameless and undisguised, as obvious and glaring as can be.

clue.text: Respectable regiment is escorted outside and dispersed

parts.note: decent means respectable
RA is the Royal Artillery, a regiment

indicators.note: outside means escorted wraps around is, enclosing it

parts.note: led means escorted

explanation.surface: A decent regiment is accompanied outside and then broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' has the escort's letters wrap around 'is', which the clue gives as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Decentralised means moved away from one centre and spread out, so dispersed.

clue.text: Scene of chaos finally disturbing Sackville-West

indicators.note: disturbing here means breaking into, so a letter is placed inside the name

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer and garden designer

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word chaos is taken

explanation.surface: A scene of disorder upsets the famous writer and gardener of Sissinghurst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' puts S inside VITA, the first name of the writer Vita Sackville-West.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a view or prospect, the scene laid out before you.

clue.text: Game to pen an ode, oddly, or another poem

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the game's letters go around the others

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports player tries to write an odd ode, or perhaps some other kind of poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts as a pick of alternate letters, but here it shuffles all of 'an ode', which 'to pen' then places inside the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain, so it is a poem other than an ode.

clue.text: Rich man angry about drug going round university

indicators.note: going round means the whole lot encloses the next letter
about means surrounding, so the word for angry goes round the drug

parts.note: cross means angry
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is furious about drugs circulating around a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside CROSS for CROESS; 'going round' then puts U inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus was a fabulously wealthy king of Lydia, and his name is a byword for a rich man.

clue.text: First barrier's best, somehow, to minimise one's risk

parts.note: a hedge is a barrier, so the first one is jokily hedge one, and with the 's it reads as a possessive

indicators.note: somehow means by some unexplained means, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that the leading obstacle is the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First barrier's' is read whimsically as barrier number one's: HEDGE ONE'S. The anagram indicator then rearranges BEST to BETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge your bets is to back more than one outcome, an idiom for limiting possible loss.

clue.text: An ace involved with this medieval league

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: the answer names this league, the Hanseatic League

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A champion player takes part in an old sporting league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges AN ACE and THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanseatic League was a medieval trading alliance of North German and Baltic towns.

clue.text: Fire consuming nothing at first, except this eatery

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word nothing

parts.note: bar means except

explanation.surface: A fire devours almost everything except one small cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames but means dismiss, SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a small place selling light meals, a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Dissenting criminal class is German, not French to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the French word at the very start of the answer

parts.note: non is French for not
a con is a convict, a criminal
a form is a school class
ist is German for is

explanation.surface: A criminal underclass described as German rather than French from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonconformist dissents from an established church or norm, so the word also works as an adjective for dissenting.

clue.text: In the centre, zlotys were sufficient for a port

indicators.note: in the centre means the middle two letters of the word zlotys

parts.note: ran to means were enough for, as funds that ran to a meal

explanation.surface: Polish money was just enough for a trip to a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The zloty is Poland's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is a port in the heel of Italy.

clue.text: Self-absorbed doctor with a whiskey in pub

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A navel-gazing doctor has a whiskey in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn means turned inwards in thought, withdrawn and introspective.

clue.text: Irishman caught at European spiritualists' meeting

parts.note: Sean is an Irish man's name
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An Irishman is spotted at a European gathering of spiritualists.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a sitting at which people try to contact the dead.

clue.text: Parting word from esteemed leader in heroic novel

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the rearranged word
novel means new, so the letters of heroic are made new by rearrangement
leader means the first letter of the word esteemed

explanation.surface: A farewell taken from a respected figure in an epic adventure novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges HEROIC to CHERIO, and E goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, a word said on parting.

clue.text: Posh theologian visiting landed earl, originally a protester

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so these letters are placed inside

parts.note: lit means landed, as a bird alights
U means upper-class, posh
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word earl

explanation.surface: A grand theologian calls on an aristocrat with an estate, who started out as a protester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' looks like the earl's estate but means alighted, LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were 19th-century workers who protested by smashing machines; the name now means anyone resisting new technology.

clue.text: Spanish island business located in Iowa

indicators.note: located in means placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa
biz is slang for business

explanation.surface: A firm based in Iowa operates on a Spanish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Continue to play, getting stick

definitions.meaning: to carry on batting in cricket
a stick, as carried by a conductor or relay runner

explanation.surface: A sportsman keeps on playing and is handed a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick; batting on is carrying on with an innings in cricket.

clue.text: Antipodean army chap embraced by Welsh girl

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the chap goes within the girl's name

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: An army man from down under is hugged by a girl from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an Australian state, so a Tasmanian comes from the Antipodes.

clue.text: Cleric's right to run round City area

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first pieces go round the area

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A clergyman claims the right to jog around a district of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' places EC inside RTOR, after its first letter. The City is London's financial district; EC is its postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a priest in charge of a parish, a kind of cleric.

clue.text: Toothless thank you note written by former PM

indicators.note: written by means the following pieces are placed after the prime minister

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister 1955-57
ta is British slang for thank you
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A thank-you letter penned by an ex-premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is a zoological term for animals lacking teeth, such as sloths and anteaters.
